The *Dutiyasekha Sutta* ("A Trainee [2nd]", Iti 17) is a short discourse in the first division of the *Itivuttaka* (PTS It 10) [SuttaCentral]. The sutta highlights friendship with admirable people (*kalyāṇamittatā*) as the foremost external factor aiding a monastic who is still in training (*sekha*) [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into multiple modern languages, including an English rendering by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

A full parallel to the discourse is preserved in the Chinese Buddhist canon as T 765.51 (善知識) [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies substantial Pali-internal reuse across six other texts (34 matching passages) [DharmaNexus]. In particular, it closely mirrors its immediately preceding companion text, the *Paṭhamasekha Sutta* (Iti 16), across segments §0.1–2.4 [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus records recurring formulaic passages shared with the *Ekakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 1, 12 matches), the *Magga Saṁyutta* (SN 45, 8 matches), the *Avijjānīvaraṇa Sutta* (Iti 14), the *Ānāpāna Saṁyutta* (SN 54), and the *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4) [DharmaNexus].
